name: Ms. Dustdevil
role: Clears away what nobody uses any more
greet.2: Tsk — who left all this lying around?
greet.4: Don't worry, I never throw anything out — it all goes into my storeroom first. You never know.
greet.5: A place for everything, and everything in its place!
fit.yes: Ms. Dustdevil is already rolling up her sleeves: "Docker? Then there's dust somewhere — I'll find it!"
fire_note: Whatever is in her storeroom stays there until you empty it — in the folders _UnraidSecretaryOffice-trash on the flash and in appdata.
check.docker: Docker is running (Ms. Dustdevil compares templates, stacks and folders with the containers)
check.docker_how: Start Docker under Settings → Docker. Without an answer from Docker every template would look unused, so she changes nothing.

section.trash_sub: Everything I put away, and where it came from. Put it back, or empty it for good.

help.order_text: Templates first, then stacks, then appdata. A folder counts as in use as long as a template or stack names it — once those are gone, it shows up here.
help.trash_text: Nothing is deleted right away. What you put away is renamed into a folder _UnraidSecretaryOffice-trash on the same disk — templates and stacks on the flash, appdata folders in the appdata share itself. That takes no time and no extra space, and "Put back" undoes it. Only "Empty" deletes for good.
help.templates_text: Leftover: no container and no image. Unused: no container, but the image is still there. Duplicate: an older file with the same <Name>. A template whose container exists is in use.
help.stacks_text: Matched with the containers by project name, the way the Compose Manager names them. Paths and images come from docker compose config, with the .env. A stack with containers is stopped (compose down) before it is put away; named volumes stay.
help.appdata_text: A folder is in use as soon as something names it: a container's mount, any template, a stack (with its .env), a compose file outside the Compose Manager, a VM, or any file on the flash (User Scripts, plugin settings …). A container that mounts the whole share doesn't count.
help.check_text: Nothing uses it, but: something has the same name, it is only mentioned in caches or the shell history, or something was written there in the last 30 days.
help.sizes_text: I count files and sizes in the background — folders to look at on my own, folders in use when you ask. Sleeping disks stay asleep; "Wake & look" wakes them when you want.
help.safe_text: While a backup runs I change nothing. I only ever rename — where that isn't possible (another disk, a dataset of its own) I refuse instead of copying.

fit.nothing: Ms. Dustdevil looked around: without Docker and without VMs there's nothing for her to sweep up. "How tidy!", she said, almost disappointed.
asleep: Part of it may be on sleeping disks ({disks}) — I didn't look there.

park.in_use_vms: Still in use: {names}. The VM won't find it any more until you put it back.
park.where_vms: Folders and disk images stay on their pool, in _UnraidSecretaryOffice-trash of their share; NVRAM, TPM states and snapshot lists in libvirt.img (/etc/libvirt/_UnraidSecretaryOffice-trash). Put back any time until you empty the storeroom.
park.zfs: ZFS datasets are renamed next to the storeroom (_UnraidSecretaryOffice-trash-<time>-<name>) — at once, with their snapshots.
zfs_text: A ZFS dataset of its own: {name}
zfs_note: A ZFS dataset of its own: I put it away with zfs rename — it then lies next to the storeroom, with its snapshots. Emptying destroys it, snapshots included.
d.used_by_none_vm: Nothing names it — no VM, container, template or file on the flash would miss it.
vms.off: The VM service isn't running (or libvirt.img isn't mounted). Without it I can't tell what belongs to a VM, so I leave everything alone.
vms.isos: Disk images in share "{share}": {places} — only .iso, .img, .qcow2 and the like; the other files there are yours.
lv.nvram_text: The VM's UEFI settings (boot entries, Secure Boot).
lv.tpm_text: The VM's virtual TPM (Windows 11, BitLocker keys).
lv.snapshotdb_text: Unraid's list of a VM's snapshots.
lv.snapshot_text: The NVRAM copy a VM snapshot made.
lv.orphan_text: No VM with this UUID or name exists any more.
img.dangling_text: An image without a name: left over when a newer version was pulled. Nothing can use it any more.
img.pull_again: No container uses it. If you need it again, Docker pulls it anew.
note.named_by_text: Named by {names} — setting it up again would pull the image anew.
note.stack_text: Belongs to the Compose stack {name} — it needs it again when it starts.
note.stack_gone_text: Belonged to the Compose project {name}, which no longer exists.
vol.anonymous_text: Made by a container on its own, without a name — usually left over after the container was removed.
vol.data_text: No container mounts it. What's inside is gone for good once it is removed.
cache.name: Build cache
cache.text: Layers docker build kept for later builds. Only what no image needs is removed (docker builder prune).
docker.note: Docker can't rename these, so they don't go into my storeroom: removing is for good. Images can be pulled again, volumes can't.
docker.cache_at: Asked Docker about its build cache {when}.

remove.volumes.other: {n} volumes can hold data (often databases) — they are gone afterwards.

why.vm_off_text: Without the VM service I can't tell what belongs to a VM.
help.vms_text: Folders in the domains share no VM uses; NVRAM files, TPM states and snapshot lists of deleted VMs (in libvirt.img); disk images in the isos share no VM has inserted. Only while the VM service runs. NVRAM copies of an existing VM's snapshots belong to Ms. Snapshotini.
help.docker_text: Dangling images (left over from updates), tagged images no container uses, volumes no container mounts, the build cache. Docker can't rename them, so they are removed for good — never while a container still uses them.
errors.cleanup_vm_off: The VM service isn't running — I won't touch {name} without it.
